          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 2.27 active sessions, 18.67% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 2.27 active sessions, 18.67% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.54 active sessions, 12.63% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.54 active sessions, 12.63% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.54 active sessions, 12.63% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "500" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 3: Top SQL Statements
Impact is 1.19 active sessions, 9.76% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .51 active sessions, 4.2% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 2% for SQL execution,
      33% for parsing, 65% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.

   Recommendation 2: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .43 active sessions, 3.53% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "8as8s1k2fhhqb" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 8as8s1k2fhhqb.
         BEGIN PKG_CBVER02_FRDRTGSFL.READ_FILES(:1,:2,:3,:4,:5); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 0% for SQL execution,
      0% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 100% for Java execution.
   Rationale
      SQL statement with SQL_ID "8as8s1k2fhhqb" was executed 13 times and had
      an average elapsed time of 89 seconds.
   Rationale
      Waiting for event "OJVM: Generic" in wait class "Other" accounted for
      100% of the database time spent in processing the SQL statement with
      SQL_ID "8as8s1k2fhhqb".

   Recommendation 3: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .25 active sessions, 2.03% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the INSERT statement with SQL_ID
      "dx303wcjkh0bg".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID dx303wcjkh0bg.
         INSERT INTO GLBNWS.TMPCERTINTTDS40(PANNO,LINKGMST,GMST_CODE,SHR_ACMCD
         ,SHR_ACNO,FRM60_61,NOTDEDRSN)

      an average elapsed time of 1.4 seconds.


Finding 4: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is .73 active sessions, 6% of total activity.
----------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .73 active sessions, 6% of total activity.
   ---------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 104 K and
      the average time per write was 1 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 28 M per second for reads
      and 55 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 65% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 34% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
